values.note: Camping on a Virginia WMA needs a written camping authorization ($10, up to six people) from Go Outdoors Virginia or a license agent, which sets the trip's start and end dates; 14 nights at most. Only in previously cleared spots, and 'unlawful to camp within 300 feet of any lake or facility'. DWR: 'WMA roads are not suitable for long vehicles or trailers ... Some WMAs may not allow travel trailers or RVs.' Hog Island WMA: 'Primitive camping and horseback riding are allowed on the Carlisle Tract ONLY.' The WMA page posts hours of 'Sunrise until sunset' (all areas open daily March 16-August 31; September closed Labor Day and Saturdays until noon; October 1-March 15 open Sundays, main road only) without saying how they apply to campers holding an authorization.

summary: Confirmed on DWR's Hog Island page that primitive camping is still allowed (Carlisle Tract only), and from DWR's statewide camping page: no hookups, no water/dump/restrooms, 14-night limit, $10 camping authorization; the WMA's posted hours added to booking.note. Not stated: season for camping, designated camping spots. Note left as is (the DWR fee line says what the inherited all-in rate cannot).
flags: Waterfront re-audit lead: entry is bayfront (AWH firsthand: 'camping areas along a dedicated fishing beach'). DWR's statewide rule (https://dwr.virginia.gov/camping-on-wmas/) says 'It is unlawful to camp within 300 feet of any lake or facility (building, boat ramp, etc.)'. The James River shore is not a lake, so the rule does not plainly bar the beach, but the Carlisle Tract's only named facility is its boat ramp at Lawnes Creek ('A road across the length of the Carlisle Tract gives access to interior parking areas and the boat ramp'); a camping area at or beside that ramp lot would be unlawful. The WMA page names no camping area.

Posted hours (info): the Hog Island WMA page lists 'Hours: Sunrise until sunset' plus seasonal restrictions (October 1-March 15 'Open Sundays, main road only'); it does not say whether they bind authorized campers on the Carlisle Tract. Worth a call to DWR (804-367-1000) before relying on off-season overnight access.
inclusion_evidence says the Go Outdoors VA authorization is 'free'; DWR's camping page says 'The fee for a camping authorization is $10' (the note already says $10).
